title: One Volcano Erupted in 1815 and Canceled the Summer of 1816

scenes.text: A volcano once erupted so hard it canceled summer.
In April 1815, Mount Tambora in Indonesia blew off the top third of its mountain.
The blast was heard 1,600 miles away.
Its ash cooled the planet. In June 1816, snow fell in New York and Maine.
Crops failed across Europe and North America.
One mountain. One whole summer, gone.

description:
Mount Tambora erupted in April 1815 and the ash cooled the planet, so 1816 became known as the year without a summer.
Snow fell in New York and Maine in June.
Could a volcano do it again?
first_comment: One volcano. A summer without summer. Which strange weather year would you want to hear about next?
